item.title: Andrej Karpathy
item.description: AI researcher and former Tesla/OpenAI lead who pioneered the LLM-maintained personal knowledge base workflow using markdown wikis and Obsidian.

item.title: ChromaDB
item.description: An open-source embedding database used in Gallagher's Knowledge Graph Kit to provide semantic vector search over graph nodes alongside SQLite structural storage.

item.title: DAIR.AI
item.description: An AI education and research organization whose Academy published the definitive system architecture analysis of Karpathy's LLM knowledge base methodology.

item.title: Dataview
item.description: An Obsidian community plugin that enables database-like queries over markdown file frontmatter, useful for dynamic views of LLM-maintained wiki metadata.

item.title: Elvis Saravia
item.description: Founder of DAIR.AI Academy who provided the most thorough system architecture analysis of Karpathy's LLM knowledge base, coining the 'four-phase operational cycle' framework.

item.title: FAISS
item.description: Facebook AI Similarity Search -- an open-source library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors, supporting billions of vectors with disk-based indexing.

item.title: FreshWiki
item.description: An evaluation dataset of recent Wikipedia articles created after LLM training cutoffs, introduced by the STORM project to prevent data leakage in automated wiki generation benchmarks.

item.title: Graphiti
item.description: An open-source framework by Zep for building temporal context graphs where facts have validity windows, designed for AI agents operating in dynamic environments.

item.title: KARMA
item.description: A NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight paper presenting a nine-agent LLM framework for automated knowledge graph enrichment from unstructured scientific text.

item.title: Marp
item.description: A markdown-based presentation framework used within Obsidian to render LLM-generated slide decks as one of the multi-format output options in the knowledge base workflow.

item.title: Matplotlib
item.description: A Python plotting library used in the LLM-KB workflow to generate data visualizations that are saved as images and viewed within Obsidian alongside wiki articles.

item.title: Memex
item.description: Vannevar Bush's 1945 vision of a personal knowledge device with associative cross-referencing -- the conceptual ancestor of hypertext, wikis, and LLM-maintained knowledge bases.

item.title: Obsidian
item.description: A markdown-based knowledge management application used as the read-only frontend IDE for LLM-maintained wikis in Karpathy's workflow.

item.title: pgvector
item.description: A PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search, widely regarded as sufficient for most team-scale retrieval use cases without requiring dedicated vector database infrastructure.

item.title: SQLite
item.description: A lightweight, serverless relational database used as the structural storage layer in Gallagher's Knowledge Graph Kit for personal knowledge management.

item.title: Steph Ango
item.description: CEO of Obsidian who recommended vault separation as a strategy to prevent LLM hallucination contamination in personal knowledge bases.

item.title: STORM
item.description: A research system for automated Wikipedia-style article creation using multi-perspective question-asking and retrieval-based outline synthesis.

item.title: Vannevar Bush
item.description: American engineer and science administrator who envisioned the Memex in 1945 -- a proto-hypertext personal knowledge device that prefigured modern LLM knowledge bases by 80 years.

item.title: Zep
item.description: The organization behind Graphiti, offering both an open-source temporal context graph engine and enterprise-grade managed infrastructure for AI agent memory.

item.title: Automated Wiki Creation
item.description: STORM's approach: single-shot, multi-perspective Wikipedia-style article generation from web search using simulated expert conversations and outline-first synthesis — contrasting with Karpathy's incremental, accumulating KB model.
